headline: Dry, warmer weather with possible morning fog lasts through Friday, then cooler, unsettled weather with light rain returns Saturday into early next week.
summary: High pressure is building over the Northwest through Friday, bringing clearing skies and a warm, dry stretch. Highs should reach the upper 60s to low 70s on Thursday and the mid 70s on Friday. Forecasters note some Minor HeatRisk both days, meaning the warmth could affect a small number of people who are especially sensitive to heat. Because the lower atmosphere is moist and winds are light, low cloud and possibly fog could form Thursday morning, though fog is described only as a possibility. Winds blowing from the east, away from the coast, could get a bit breezy in the Cascades and foothills Thursday night, with gusts of 25-30 mph. Humidity in the Cascades and southern Olympics could drop to around 35-40% Thursday and 35-45% Friday. The weather turns over the weekend as the high pressure weakens and a series of weak systems move through. Saturday will likely bring rain during the day, mostly in the North Cascades, with only a few hundredths of an inch in the lowlands and some Seattle-area spots possibly staying dry. The bigger change is temperature, with highs falling to the low 60s on Saturday. Sunday should be cooler and drier, with morning lows in the low 40s around Puget Sound and the mid 30s in the Cascade foothills. Cool, unsettled weather continues into early next week, with more chances for light rain, especially Tuesday. Forecasters are fairly confident in the warm, dry stretch and the Saturday turn, but the track of an offshore trough (a dip in the jet stream) on Sunday could change the forecast, and the pattern after Tuesday is unclear because the forecast models disagree. Seas on the coastal waters will build over the weekend and may go higher into early next week. No weather hazards are listed.
